name: Alliums
comments: Allium is a genus of plants which includes onions and garlic.

name: Beans, bush
comments: "Lettuce, potato, tomato, other legumes, crucifers, or cucurbits increase sclerotinia" in the soil and should be avoided before and after snap beans. See the entry for "Legumes" for more info

name: Beans, pole
comments: the stalk of the corn provides a pole for the beans to grow on, which then gives nitrogen to the soil of the corn. Beans and corn are (with squash) traditional "Three Sisters" plants. As for Radishes, see the entry for "Legumes".

name: Beans, fava
comments: See the entry for "Legumes" for more info

name: Beets
comments: Good for adding minerals to the soil through composting leaves which have up to 25% magnesium. Runner or pole beans and beets stunt each other's growth.

name: Brassicas
helpedBy: Aromatic plants or plants with many blossoms
comments: Brassicas are a family of plants which includes broccoli, Brussels sprouts, cabbage, cauliflower, Chinese cabbage, kohlrabi, radish, and turnip. Thyme, nasturtiums, and onion showed good resistance to cabbage worm, weevil and cabbage looper.

name: Broccoli
comments: Broccoli as a main crop intercropped with lettuce was shown to be more profitable than either crop alone. Turnip acts as a trap crop. See brassicas entry for more info

name: Cabbage
comments: See brassicas entry for more info. If using clover as an intercrop it should be sown after cabbage transplant so as not to affect crop yield. Nasturtiums repel cabbage moths

name: Carrots
attracts: Yellow jacket and other predatory wasps
comments: Tomatoes grow better with carrots, but may stunt the carrots' growth. Beans provide the nitrogen carrots need more than some other vegetables. Aromatic companion plants repel carrot fly. Alliums inter-planted with carrots confuse onion and carrot flies. For the beneficial insect-attracting properties of carrots to work, they need to be allowed to flower; Otherwise, use wild carrot, Queen Anne's Lace, for the same effect.

name: Cauliflower
comments: See brassicas for more info. See peas regarding their mutualism with cauliflower.

name: Celery
comments: Aster flowers, can transmit the aster yellows disease

name: Corn / Maize
comments: Provides beans with a trellis, is protected from predators and dryness by cucurbits, in the three sisters technique

name: Cucumber
comments: Sow 2 or 3 radish seeds in with cucumbers to repel cucumber beetles. One study showed a 75% reduction in cucumber beetles with the concurrent seeding of amaranth. Various sprays from lettuce, asparagus, Malabar spinach, and celery were found to reduce whiteflies. See cucurbits entry for more info

name: Cucurbits
comments: Cucurbits are a family of plants that includes melons, cucumbers, gourds, pumpkins, and squash

name: Eggplant or Aubergine
comments: Marigolds will deter nematodes.

name: Kohlrabi
comments: See Brassicas entry for more info

name: Leek
comments: See Alliums entry for more info

name: Legumes
comments: Hosts nitrogen-fixing bacteria, a good fertiliser for some plants, too much for others. Rosemary and peppermint extracts are used in organic sprays for beans. Summer savory and potatoes repel bean beetles.

name: Lettuce
comments: Broccoli when intercropped with lettuce was shown to be more profitable than either crop alone.

name: Mustard
comments: See Brassicas entry.

name: Nightshades
comments: Nightshades are a family of plants which include tomatoes, tobacco, chili peppers (including bell peppers), potatoes, eggplant, and others

name: Okra
comments: Okra and sweet potato are mutually beneficial when planted simultaneously.

name: Onion
comments: See Alliums entry for more info

name: Parsnip
comments: The flowers of the parsnip plant left to seed will attract a variety of predatory insects to the garden, they are particularly helpful when left under fruit trees, the predators attacking codling moth and light brown apple moth.

name: Peas
comments: Peas when intercropped with turnips, cauliflower, or garlic showed mutual suppression of growth however their profit per land area used was increased.

name: Peppers
comments: Pepper plants like high humidity, which can be helped along by planting with some kind of dense-leaf or ground-cover companion, like marjoram and basil; pepper plants grown together, or with tomatoes, can shelter the fruit from excess sunlight, and raise the humidity level. Sunflowers, when in bloom at the right time, shelter beneficial insects, lowering thrips populations.

name: Potato
comments: Horseradish increases the disease resistance of potatoes. It repels the potato bug. Garlic is more effective than fungicides on late potato blight. Peas were shown to reduce the density of Colorado potato beetles.

name: Pumpkin
helps: In trad. three sisters partnership beans
comments: Radishes can be used as a trap crop against flea beetles, cucurbita can be used in the Three Sisters technique. Nasturtiums repel squash bugs.

name: Radish
comments: Radishes can be used as a trap crop against flea beetles. Radishes grown with lettuce taste better.

name: Soybean
comments: A mixture of corn, mungbean, and sunflower was found to rid soybeans of aphids.

name: Spinach
comments: The peas and beans provide natural shade for the spinach. See cauliflower notes regarding mutualism with spinach.

name: Squash
comments: Radishes can be used as a trap crop against flea beetles, cucurbita can be used in the three sisters technique. Marigolds and nasturtiums repel squash bugs. Marigolds repel cucumber beetles.

name: Sweet potato
comments: Okra and sweet potato are mutually beneficial when planted simultaneously.

name: Tomatoes
comments: Black walnuts inhibit tomato growth, in fact they are negative allelopathic to all other nightshade plants (chili pepper, potato, tobacco, petunia) as well, because it produces a chemical called juglone. Dill attracts tomato hornworm.Growing tomatoes with Basil does not appear to enhance tomato flavour but studies have shown that growing them around 10 inches apart can increase the yield of tomatoes by about 20%. One study shows that growing chili peppers near tomatoes in greenhouses increases tomato whitefly on the tomatoes.Cucumbers and squash can be used as living mulch, or green mulch, around tomato plants. The large leaves of these vining plants can help with soil moisture retention.

name: Turnips and rutabagas
comments: Turnips act as a trap crop for broccoli. See peas regarding their mutualism with turnips.

name: Apple
avoid: Cedar because of apple-cedar rust. walnut because its roots produce growth inhibitors that apple trees are sensitive to
comments: French marigold inhibits codling moth but also its insect enemies, and fails to reduce damage to apples.

name: Apricot
comments: A fungus that peppers are prone to can infect apricot trees causing a lot of harm.

name: Blueberries
comments: Pine and oak trees create the acidic soil blueberries need. Strawberries and dewberries create healthy ground cover, clover fixes nitrogen for the blueberries' high needs, yarrow and bay laurel repel unhealthy insects. Each of the herbal companions listed also like the acidic soil the blueberry plant needs.

name: Strawberries
comments: Thyme planted and/or placed next to each other help grow more strawberries quickly.

name: Anise
comments: Not to be confused with star anise which is an entirely different species.

name: Basil
comments: Is said to make tomatoes taste better, chamomile and anise are supposed to increase the essential oils in many herbs like basil

name: Borage
comments: Predict a square metre for its adult size. Borage is a good companion for a wide variety of plants.

name: Chamomile
comments: Growing near herbs will increase their oil production.

name: Chervil
comments: Loves shade, fortunately it grows well with shade-tolerant food plants; will make radishes grown near it taste spicier

name: Chives
comments: Same companion traits as all alliums (onions, garlic, shallots, leeks, etc.)said to prevent apple scab after 3 years planting at base of apple trees

name: Cilantro / Coriander
comments: Attracts hoverflies which may in turn reduce pest populations in cabbages.

name: Dill
comments: One of the few plants said to grow with fennel: See fennel for info about intercropping.

name: Fennel
comments: Fennel is allelopathic to most garden plants, inhibiting growth, causing to bolt, or actually killing many plants. When growing together a higher ratio of fennel to dill provides the highest profit. Dill has a stabilizing effect on the fennel seed. Because it attracts syrphidae it reduces aphids through predation.

name: Flax
comments: Flax contains tannin and linseed oils which may offend the Colorado potato bug

name: Garlic
comments: See Alliums entry for more info. Peas and garlic when planted closely together suppress each other's growth; however the profit over land area used is higher. Tarragon makes garlic grow rapidly.

name: Hyssop
comments: Stimulates growth of grapes.

name: Lavender
scientificName: Lavandula angustifolia, L. dentata, L. stoechas

name: Lemon grass
comments: Reduces cutworms in eggplant in laboratory trials

name: Lovage
comments: Is thought to improve the health of almost all plants, like borage and geraniums, is considered a "magic bullet" of companion planting

name: Oregano
comments: Provides ground cover and much-needed humidity for pepper plants if allowed to spread among them. Because it attracts syrphidae, it reduces aphids through predation.

name: Parsley
comments: Sacrificially attracts insects that feed on tomatoes

name: Peppermint
comments: Repels cabbage flies, has same general companion properties as other mints

name: Rosemary
comments: Deters cabbage flies, repels many bean parasites

name: Sage
avoid: Avoid any member of the allium family and common rue

name: Southernwood
comments: Controls cabbage moths and malaria mosquitoes.

name: Spearmint
comments: Controls ants and aphids.

name: Summer savoury
comments: Also delays germination of certain foul herbs

name: Tarragon
comments: Its scent is disliked by most pests, and this plant is also thought to have Nurse Plant properties, enhancing the growth and flavor of crops grown with it.

name: Thyme
comments: Because it attracts Syrphidae, it reduces aphids through predation.

name: Wormwood
comments: Wormwood should be used with caution around most vegetables since it contains toxins.

name: Yarrow
comments: May increase the essential oil production of some herbs. Also improves soil quality, use the leaves to enrich compost, or as mulch. Because it attracts syrphidae it reduces aphids through predation.

name: Alyssum
comments: Because they attract syrphidae they help reduce aphids through predation.

name: Baby's breath
comments: Because they attract Syrphidae, they help reduce aphids through predation.

name: Californian poppy
comments: Because they attract Syrphidae, they help reduce aphids through predation.

name: Geraniums
comments: A trap crop, attracting pests away from roses and grape vines, distracts beet leafhoppers, carrier of the curly top virus, keep away from solanaceous plants like eggplant, and tobacco

name: Lupin
comments: This wildflower is a legume, hosting bacteria that fixes nitrogen in the soil, fertilizing it for neighboring plants. Same with marigold, planting nearby roses causes them to grow vigorously.

name: Marigold
scientificName: Tagetes patula, T. erecta, T. minuta
comments: Marigolds are a wonder-drug of the companion plant world, invoking the saying "plant them everywhere in your garden". French marigolds (T. patula) produce a pesticidal chemical from their roots, so strong it lasts years after they are gone. Mexican marigolds (T. erecta) do the same, but are so strong they will inhibit the growth of some more tender herbs. Stinking Roger (T. minuta) has also been found effective against certain perennial weeds. Same with lupin, planting nearby roses causes them to grow vigorously.

name: Nasturtium
comments: Trap crops for aphids, is among the best at attracting predatory insects, deters many pests of cucurbits

name: Pansy
comments: A good and nice-smelling flower that really attracts ants. It is like the viola plant, but has two or three colors in flowers. Helps alliums and onions, which repels the white butterfly.

name: Petunia
comments: Is a trap crop almost identical to geraniums in function

name: Phacelia
helps: Plants which are prone to aphids
comments: This plant attracts hoverflies and is good around plants which are prone to aphids.

name: Sunflower
comments: Was grown as a companion for corn (maize) before modern Europeans arrived in the Americas, supposedly increases their production, ants herd aphids onto sunflowers, keeping them off neighboring plants. Works as a trap plant for thrips keeping them off of bell peppers. Planting near swan plants help sunflowers grow rapidly.

name: Swan plant
avoid: Plants that attracts aphids and spider mites
comments: Attracts the monarch butterfly during spring and summer. Basil repels pests that attracts by the swan plant like aphids.

name: Sweet pea
comments: An annual climbing plant, which is like the edible pea. Makes a good decoration in your garden or fence.

name: Tansy
comments: Toxic to people and many animals; do not plant it where livestock browse. Is reputed to repel herbivorous insects.

name: Zinnia
comments: Attracts hummingbirds that eat whiteflies, attracts pollinators

name: Alfalfa
comments: Used by farmers to reduce cotton pests, a good crop to improve soil; fixes nitrogen. Alfalfa has some allelopathic effects to tomato seedlings.

name: Peanut
comments: Peanuts encourage growth of corn and squash

name: Walnut tree
comments: Black walnut is harmful to the growth of all nightshade plants, including Datura or Jimson weed, eggplant, mandrake, deadly nightshade or belladonna, capsicum (paprika, chile pepper), potato, tomato, and petunia.
